turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I've been digging into knowledge graph embeddings. It's interesting how TransE models triples as h + r ≈ t in a shared embedding space using L1/L2 scoring.
That is a fundamental concept in KG embeddings. The translational distance property makes it quite efficient for large graphs.
Exactly. It's simple but effective. By the way, do you remember if I ordered that replacement fan for my laptop yet?
I don't have access to your purchase history in this chat, so I can't confirm the order status. Did you check your email?
Ah, right. I'll check later. It's been so hot here, the laptop is running hot anyway. Any tips on cooling it down?
Elevating the back of the laptop and cleaning the vents with compressed air can help significantly.
Good idea. I'll try that. Thanks, Lloyd.
Lloyd, I saw something new in robotics. LingBot-VLA surpasses π₀.5 on AgiBot G1 tasks using only ~80 demonstrations per task compared to π₀.5's 130.
That is a significant reduction in data requirements. Few-shot learning in vision-language-action models is really advancing.
Yeah, it makes deployment way more practical. Speaking of practical, did you remember to remind me about the dentist appointment?
I don't have calendar access to set reminders for you, Alan. You might want to check your own calendar app.
Right, right. I always forget. The weather is supposed to be rain-free this weekend, so maybe I'll ride my bike there.
That sounds like a good plan if the forecast holds up. Enjoy the ride.
